parameters.content:
## Bottle Defect Classifier - End-to-End Workflow

This n8n graph is a **documentation / visualization artifact**, not a runnable automation.
It mirrors the real pipeline implemented across `calibrate.py`, `dataset.py`, `train.py`,
`infer.py`, `bench.py` and the `gui.py` tabs (Label, Defects, Train, Analysis, Live,
Camera, Data health, Settings).

Each node's *Notes* field cites the exact file/function/line that implements that step,
so this file can be read alongside CLAUDE.md as a visual index of the system.

Data backbone: `projects/<slug>/labels.csv` (source of truth) + `config.json`
(ROI, thresholds) + `models/<stamp>/` (checkpoints). See `dataset.py` module globals.

nodes.name: New / Open Project
nodes.notes: gui.py new_project()/switch_project() (gui.py:148-159). Calls dataset.use_project(name), which rebinds every D.* path constant to projects/<slug>/... and persists the choice to projects/active.txt. Always stops running cameras first.

nodes.name: Calibrate ROI
nodes.notes: calibrate.py, invoked standalone on first run or via DataTab 'Re-measure' (gui.py:1150, calibrate.run()). Measures the bottle crop box using Sobel edge-energy row/column profiles (_span, calibrate.py:22), thresholded relative to their own floor/peak. Unions the middle 95% of ~60 sampled frames to avoid one bad frame blowing out the box. Writes roi=[x,y,w,h] + roi_frame=[W,H] into projects/<slug>/config.json.

nodes.name: Label Images
nodes.notes: gui.py LabelTab (gui.py:198). Paginated thumbnail grid, filter by mode (all/inbox/good/defective/pos/neg), multi-select with keyboard shortcuts (1-9 toggle defect, g=good, a=select page, Esc=clear). Bulk apply/clear/delete via D.apply_labels/D.delete_images. On load, dataset.sync_new_images (dataset.py:245) reconciles the images/ folders into labels.csv WITHOUT ever overwriting an existing row, so folder position only seeds a label the first time an image is imported.

nodes.name: Manage Defect Classes
nodes.notes: gui.py DefectsTab (gui.py:442). Add/rename/delete defect classes = add/rename/delete a -ve/<Class>/ folder = add/rename/delete a labels.csv column. rename_defect() renames the folder and the column together (a stale folder resurrects the old label on rescan otherwise). Deleting a class drops the column and moves its images to _inbox/ (reviewed=0), never to 'good'. Shows per-class counts with a 'thin - aim for 100+' warning.

nodes.name: Train Model
nodes.notes: TrainTab 'Train now' (gui.py:601) spawns a thread calling train.run(epochs, log=emit). EfficientNet-B0 backbone (ImageNet-pretrained), one multi-label linear head, BCEWithLogitsLoss with per-column pos_weight=clip(neg/pos,1,50). Augmentation: rotation/scale/brightness/contrast jitter, NO horizontal flip (would mirror label text / invert skew direction). Split is by detected scene (dataset.scene_map/split_train_val, dataset.py:630-704), not random, to avoid near-duplicate frame leakage between train/val. A defect with 0 training positives gets threshold=1.01 (unreachable) and is disabled. Writes projects/<slug>/models/<stamp>/{model.pt, labels.csv snapshot, metrics.json (incl. val_paths)}.

nodes.name: Evaluate & Compare Checkpoints
nodes.notes: gui.py AnalysisTab (gui.py:1303), charts drawn on a plain Tk Canvas (charts.py, no matplotlib). Loss/macro-F1 curves, per-defect recall bars, confusion matrix per defect. compare()/show_compare() re-tests every saved checkpoint against today's labels.csv via train.score_checkpoint(), which refuses to score a checkpoint that never recorded val_paths, and flags checkpoints that predate the current val split as 'needs retrain' vs honestly re-scored.

nodes.name: Activate Checkpoint
nodes.notes: TrainTab activate() (gui.py:726). Selects a models/<stamp>/ checkpoint as the live one and derives per-defect thresholds from that checkpoint's own metrics.json. infer.Model (infer.py:77) always crops using the ROI/input size baked INTO the checkpoint, not the project's live config.json - this is what makes rolling back to an older model safe even if the camera/ROI has since changed.

nodes.name: Live Multi-Camera Inference
nodes.notes: gui.py LiveTab (gui.py:772). infer.CameraSet (infer.py:292) shares one Model across N cameras, one background grab thread each, always infers on the NEWEST frame (mid-inference arrivals are dropped and counted, never queued -> bounded latency). Capped ~15Hz per camera regardless of source FPS. Per-camera PASS/FAIL overlay + real-time FPS/latency/drop% (Camera.stats() + bench.system_stats()). Per-defect threshold sliders bound live to config.json.

nodes.name: Combined Verdict (PASS/FAIL)
nodes.notes: infer.CameraSet.combined() (infer.py:360): REJECT if ANY camera rejects. Rationale: multiple angles of the same physical bottle share one verdict - a defect only one angle can see is still a defect. (If cameras instead watch independent lines, use each camera's own verdict rather than combined()).

nodes.name: Snapshot Capture -> Inbox
nodes.notes: LiveTab's snapshot-into-a-label capture panel (gui.py:772). Operator captures an interesting live frame straight into a project's images/_inbox/ (reviewed=0), closing the loop back into Label Images for the next training round - this is how the model improves over time on real line traffic.

nodes.name: Data Health Monitor
nodes.notes: gui.py DataTab 'Data health' (gui.py:1150). ROI editing (manual + Re-measure), near-duplicate-frame scan (dataset.scene_map) reporting how many DISTINCT bottles N images actually represent, plus dataset health counts (per-class thin warnings, unreviewed backlog, etc). Feeds back into deciding what still needs labeling.

nodes.name: Camera Benchmark
nodes.notes: gui.py BenchTab 'Camera' tab (gui.py:1552). bench.benchmark_camera() sweeps resolution/FPS combos, measures ACTUAL delivered FPS/latency/jitter/sharpness/inference-time (OpenCV reports the requested mode, not the achieved one). bench.best_combo() recommends a setting picked by SHARPNESS, not raw FPS - a defect the camera can't resolve is invisible at any frame rate. Guarded against running concurrently with LiveTab's cameras.

nodes.name: Settings (global)
nodes.notes: gui.py SettingsTab (gui.py:1712). App-wide UI preferences persisted to top-level settings.json (D.load_settings/save_settings, dataset.py:149-171) - NOT per-project, unlike labels.csv/config.json which live under projects/<slug>/.
